_comment: This is a hand-maintained list, not something parsed out of src/. That is
deliberate and it is the tool's central compromise: the schemas a PRD 2-6
ticket references are mostly the schemas that ticket is asking someone to
build. There is no source of truth to parse for `escalation.md` or
`awaiting-adjudication` until the slice that introduces them merges, so a
parser would report every forward reference as unknown and the lint would
be useless exactly where it is needed. See docs/adr/0049-ticket-lint.md.
What the lint therefore decides is narrower and honest: a name in an
acceptance criterion must be findable *somewhere a reader can reach* —
either in this declared list (it exists in the pipeline today) or in the
ticket's own prose (the ticket introduces it). A name in neither is a name
Adding a name here is a claim that it exists in the pipeline today. Keep it
that way: if you catch yourself adding a name to silence a finding on a
thing that does not exist yet, the fix is the ticket's prose, not this file.
_placeholderComment: One letter and a digit or two is a placeholder for an opaque runtime ID —
`F1` for a finding, `R2` for a round. #78 uses `F1` across three fixture
cases and there is nothing for it to be declared as.

absentNames.name: held
absentNames.note: There is no HELD finding state (matching here is case-insensitive, so this entry covers 'HELD' too). A finding the evaluator refuses to withdraw stays CONTESTED. Writing 'held' in a criterion invites a fifth state that no schema has.
absentNames.recordedIn: #78 (PRD1-S4), section 'Finding states': 'There is no fifth `HELD` state'

absentNames.name: rejection-cases
absentNames.note: The mandatory rejection-cases ticket field was cut in the plan debate as a forever-tax on every future ticket author. A criterion may not require it.

absentNames.name: GAPS
absentNames.note: Agent self-count markers left the negotiate stage with #77. A criterion naming them describes control flow that no longer exists.

absentNames.name: RE_RAISED_GAPS
absentNames.note: As GAPS — removed from the negotiate control flow by #77.

_channelsComment: A channel is a destination, not a payload. `the review artifact` is not on
this list on purpose: naming the thing recorded is not naming where it
lands, and the archive-location ambiguity in #77's 'every review attempt is
archived' is what #123 (stale review archives relocated on restart) cost.
A concrete artifact filename (`qa-review.json`) counts as a channel by the
filename rule in the script and needs no entry here.
